title: RingX: Scalable Parallel Attention for Long-Context Learning on HPC
problem: Long-context training requires scalable attention parallelism, but ring attention's point-to-point communication strategy fails to exploit modern HPC network architectures, limiting scalability and efficiency.
motivation: State-of-the-art models (reasoning LLMs, high-resolution image/video generators) require increasingly long context windows, but quadratic attention complexity makes training infeasible. Ring attention is suboptimal for HPC networks.
method: RingX enhances ring attention with: (1) improved workload partitioning, (2) refined communication patterns optimized for HPC networks, (3) improved load balancing, (4) optimization for bi-directional and causal attention mechanisms.
key_novelty: HPC-aware communication pattern optimization for ring attention, achieving 3.4x speedup over conventional ring attention on Frontier supercomputer.
contributions: 3.4x speedup over conventional ring attention on 64+ GPUs (Frontier supercomputer)
1.5x end-to-end training speedup for Vision Transformer and Llama3 8B
38% model FLOPs utilization (MFU) for Llama3 8B with 1M-token sequences on 4096 GPUs
Optimized for both bi-directional and causal attention
workloads: Vision Transformer training on climate data
limitations: Full-text not available; analysis based on abstract. Evaluation primarily on Frontier supercomputer; generalization to other HPC systems not discussed.
primary_theme: HPC-optimized parallel attention for long-context model training
